plan.title: Whole-blood co-expression modules linked to case/control status
plan.analytical_narrative: The research question asks which co-expression modules the 12,000 genes form across the 120 whole-blood samples (60 cases, 60 controls, single batch, unpaired) and which modules track case/control status. This requires (1) standard QC and normalization of the raw Salmon gene-level counts, (2) a population-scale-appropriate differential expression test as a complementary, per-gene view of the case/control axis, (3) the core co-expression analysis with WGCNA on the variance-stabilized matrix to define modules, compute eigengenes, and correlate eigengenes with case/control status and covariates, (4) functional characterization of the trait-associated modules against curated human pathway collections, and (5) an integrated report. Because each group holds 60 samples (>=50/group), the knowledge base flags that DESeq2/edgeR negative-binomial models exaggerate false positives in large population cohorts; limma-voom with a fixed-effects linear model is used for the per-gene DE step instead, with the caution stated in the report. WGCNA module detection is unaffected by that concern since it operates on the variance-stabilized matrix directly, not on a per-gene NB test. Reference pathway collections (MSigDB Hallmark human, Reactome, WikiPathways human) and the STRING human PPI network are confirmed present in the environment and used for module annotation; org.Hs.eg.db is confirmed present for identifier mapping.

integrated report with DE, enrichment, and coexpression-trait results
